### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a4c0841064d90f54e803f9c75e635c921cea6df8` — the merge of head `07a5f786ce8ee8da1fe3e3268690b3848848266e` into base `951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a4c0841064d90f54e803f9c75e635c921cea6df8 && git checkout a4c0841064d90f54e803f9c75e635c921cea6df8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f 07a5f786ce8ee8da1fe3e3268690b3848848266e && git checkout -B drift-repro 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f && git merge --no-ff 07a5f786ce8ee8da1fe3e3268690b3848848266e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 951eceeeec8803029966ac15c18f387d434b976f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `07a5f786ce8ee8da1fe3e3268690b3848848266e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/objectql/src/disabled-holder-packageless-row-doors.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts (cited code, read on main, never reviewed); .changeset/34144-bare-save-holder-judgment.md judged for ② only
Security-touching: no

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Read: the three cards with every comment, the PR body, file list, comments and net diff against `main`, the 51 check-runs on this head, AGENTS.md and ADR-0150 on `main`, and the cited code. Nothing was built or run; every judgment below is a reading of the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

The diff adds one judgment, `packagelessHolderRefusal`, at three call sites, each placed after the existing refusals. It only returns a refusal or `undefined`, so no answer that was refused becomes accepted. RIGHT.

Moved, accepted to refused, as the tree reads:

- Two or more enabled holders, publish save, over no row or over one package's row: 200 to `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming the enabled holders. RIGHT; it is the resolver's own refusal (`resolveItem` naming no package), the call the bare read makes in `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`.
- Same state, draft save (`?mode=draft`): 200 to 409 naming them. RIGHT.
- Same state, bare delete over one package's row: removed to 409 naming them, row stays. RIGHT.
- Every holder disabled, publish save over the disabled package's row, over no row, and at a bundled member the holder never ships (#34262): 200 to 409 with the `?package=` remedy, naming no package. RIGHT; the message is built from the verb, type and name alone.
- Same state, draft save and bare delete over the disabled package's row: 200 to 409 naming none. RIGHT.
- Row bound to a customization pair of a disabled holder: counted as that holder, as the read face's `isHoldersPairRow` withholds it. RIGHT.

Not moved, confirmed by reading:

- A write naming a package: every call site is guarded on no package named.
- The environment's own item (`getEnvironmentScopedItem`) and a package-unbound row at the address (`address.unbound`).
- One enabled holder; a name no package holds.
- A row bound to an id no installed package has: `isPackageDisabled` reads it as enabled, so the later named-base refusal still answers.
- The #32605 cells on the publish save: `servedPackagelessSaveAddress` answers first.
- Server-stated rewrites (`source` set) and `package-duplicate`.

Named WRONG or incomplete:

- The changeset says the bare delete "used to remove the one package's row". The same call also moves the bare delete and the bare draft discard over NO stored row. That path answered `success: true, reset: false` (the no-op receipt, after the registry self-heal) and now answers 409 in both states. Undeclared and unpinned: S2.
- "Every moved answer goes from accepted to refused" is not the whole motion. A bare save in these two states that a later gate refused (an invalid body, a read-only inherited package) now answers this 409 first. Still refused, and the same rank as the existing two-bindings refusal: nit N4.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`. AGENTS.md Post-Task 3: the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its banner and disposition. Correct.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: no key, accepted value or metadata type changes; the same item is still writable by naming its package. Correct.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: line-initial in the PR body and the changeset, a legal pairing, BREAKING. The BREAKING banner is in both.
- `!`: on the PR title and the changeset summary line.
- ADR-0087 marker: exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The reason holds: no schema key, export or stored row changes.
- `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are success on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev open question (a package-unbound row of a name only disabled packages ship: bare read 404, bare save 200 and hidden): ESCALATED, not answered. Ruling A's remedy does not reach a package-unbound row, and the cell is a read/write asymmetry the ruling's wording arguably covers. It needs the maintainer's word: S3.
- Dev acceptance note (two enabled holders plus a package-unbound row: bare read 409, bare save edits the row): the same class, escalated in the same card: S3.
- Dev flag "dogfood battery owed again on the final head": the dev's reading is at `6401aad2f3` and no later report is on the cards. On this head the required `Dogfood Regression Gate` context is success; PR runs skip the shards and the queue run adds them (AGENTS.md, two speeds). The PR's own source hunks are unchanged since the measured head. Answered: the queue run carries it.
- Dev deviations (pins added to the shared #32605 harness, `put` gained a query argument; unpushed amend before the first push): accepted, no contract effect.
- Out-of-scope carrier #33995: resolved on this head. #33995 is merged, `main` is merged in, and the S3 save pin is flipped with its delete half and shipped-member CONTROL kept.
- All 51 check-runs on this head: success or skipped, none failed.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The one new store read is `packagelessAddress` at `active` on the draft path, a `WHERE type, name, state` read. The unions are over holder ids from the in-memory registry; no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away. ADR-0150 D5 on `main`: a bare address resolves while the name has one holder and answers 409 otherwise, "never a silent pick", with no new code minted. D3: a caller with no package gets the environment's item first, else the unique holder, else the refusal. The save and delete now give that answer through the read's own resolver call, with the existing `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`. The disabled-only arm rests on ruling A on #34144 and the registry's served-holder rule (#32183), not on ADR text: N3.

Does the write door count holders as the bare read does, cell by cell:

- Environment's own item: yes, the same `getEnvironmentScopedItem` test; left alone.
- `?package=` writes: not judged, unchanged.
- Single enabled holder: yes, the resolver resolves and the disabled-only test finds an enabled id.
- Two or more enabled holders, no disabled binding among the rows: yes, on publish save, draft save and delete.
- Mixed, publish save, one enabled and one disabled holder: yes, by #32605's step, untouched.
- Mixed, publish save, two enabled holders and a disabled binding among the rows: NO in one sub-cell, S1.
- Mixed, draft save and delete: NO, unchanged from `main`. Neither door has the #32605 step, so both take the address from the rows: the disabled holder's row is written or removed while the read serves the enabled holder. Over a row of each, the delete's 409 names the disabled package. Folded into S1's follow-up.
- Types the registry does not read by package (`action`, `doc`, whose bare reads refuse through their own judges): not judged here. The PR body says so; the changeset's "Not moved" list does not: N4.

Leak check on the disabled-only refusal: it names no package. `disabledHoldersOnlyRefusal` takes only the verb, the shown type and the name; the delete rethrows it as it is. It does disclose that some disabled package holds the name (409 where a free name saves), which is inherent to ruling A.

S1 (should-fix) — one cell of #33955 survives on the publish save, by reading. State: two enabled packages E and F hold the name, and the stored rows are bound to a disabled package and to exactly one enabled package (E). `servedPackagelessSaveAddress` reads no served address, sees the disabled binding, keeps the one enabled binding and returns E. The new judgment sits in the other branch and is never asked. The save writes E's row (200); the bare read refuses 409 naming E and F. Unchanged from `main` and outside the cards' measured states, so not a regression. Either ask the resolver arm before the enabled-bindings pick, or file the follow-up card with the mixed delete and draft cells before `Fixes #33955` closes the card. Until then the helper's jsdoc ("answer the name as the bare read does") overclaims.

S2 (should-fix) — declare and pin the no-row delete. A bare delete or bare draft discard over no stored row moves from the no-op success receipt to 409 in both states. Add the FROM-TO to the changeset and one pin per state, or guard the delete call on a row being addressed.

S3 (should-fix) — file the decision card for the package-unbound-row cells (③): beside a disabled-only name (read 404, save 200 hidden) and beside two enabled holders (read 409, save 200).

- N1 (nit): the new catch uses `instanceof PackageScopedNameRefusedError` alone. The package's own recogniser `packageScopedRefusalOf` also reads the shape across a copied class. A copy would rethrow the resolver's 409 without the save remedy; still refused.
- N2 (nit): the disabled-only delete pins assert code and status only, not the `?package=` remedy or that no package is named. Delete pins go through the protocol, not the two transports.
- N3 (nit): the changeset cites ADR-0150 D3 for "a disabled package holds no name". ADR-0150 on `main` has no such sentence; the authority is ruling A and the registry rule of #32183.
- N4 (nit): two changeset wordings. "Still refused `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`" for a shipped member holds only where the package door refuses; in the runtime harness that save moved 200 to 409. The "Not moved" list omits the types not read by package and the refused-to-refused code moves in ①.
- N5 (nit): the draft path reads the active rows for every bare draft save before asking whether the type is read by package. The PR is still marked draft and its body still carries the "Waits on #33995" banner, stale at this head.

No must-fix.
